entries.title: Psalms 50:1
segments: In this psalm God is represented as coming forth in majesty and glory from his dwelling place in mount Zion, and summoning his covenant people to judgment for their hypocrisy and wickedness.

entries.title: Psalms 50:2
segments: The perfection of beauty; Zion, as the royal abode of Jehovah, was to the pious Israelite the sum of all excellence and beauty.

entries.title: Psalms 50:3
segments:
Shall come; from Zion to judge his people. 
 
A day is coming when all shall discern between him that serveth God in truth, and him that serveth him not.

entries.title: Psalms 50:4
segments: Call to the heavens--to the earth; to heaven and earth with all their inhabitants, to be present as witnesses.

entries.title: Psalms 50:5
segments: My saints; my visible, professed worshippers.  Israel, as the peculiar people of God, and consecrated to his service, is called "a holy nation,"

. 
 
  By sacrifice; the national covenant with Israel was originally ratified by sacrifices and the sprinkling of blood,
; and the stated sacrifices appointed under the law, may be regarded as a perpetual renewing of this covenant.

entries.title: Psalms 50:6
segments: His righteousness; the correctness of his decisions.

entries.title: Psalms 50:8
segments: External service merely, without the heart being engaged, will be of no avail in the sight of God.

entries.title: Psalms 50:9
segments: I will take no bullock; God does not require sacrifices, or any other services which men can render, for his own sake, "as though he needed any thing," nor will he accept them unless offered in faith and love.

entries.title: Psalms 50:14
segments: Thanksgiving; a spiritual service: not that thanksgiving should be substituted for sacrifice, but that these should be an expression of thanksgiving.

entries.title: Psalms 50:15
segments: Humble, believing, affectionate prayer will always be heard, and in God's own way and time be abundantly answered.

entries.title: Psalms 50:16
segments:
The wicked; the open violators of God's law. 
 
God will not accept any service at the hand of the habitual violators of his law.

entries.title: Psalms 50:21
segments: Such a one as thyself; one who would connive at wickedness, and suffer it to go unpunished.

entries.title: Psalms 50:22
segments:
Tear you in pieces; suddenly and utterly destroy you. 
 
God often waits upon sinners with much long-suffering, but will finally call them to account, and punish them according to their deserts.

entries.title: Psalms 50:23
segments: Offereth praise; offers sacrifices of thanksgiving. See

. 
 
Without an upright life, all professions of godliness, and all claims to true religion and salvation are vain.
